screeningRules: Preserve aspiration; exclude oral/nasal mismatch, including lost nasal codas.
Treat nasalized vowels as nasal codas.
Open single-syllable candidates require exact onset and close rime; no gloss-substring recall.
Explicit exclusions and rejected donor words override phonetic similarity.
Whole-word loans only: do not flag compounds solely for a Chinese component.

brassettLabialReview.source: Brassett, Brassett & Lu 2006, The Tujia Language
brassettLabialReview.verified: Section 2.1 describes /x/ as [x] in all environments and gives [xu21] for drink. Table 2.34 maps h to [x], with hu3 drink as its example. Neither table uses ɸ.
brassettLabialReview.editorialConversion: For hua/huai/huan/hui/huo, hu corresponds to f without a repeated u medial. Standalone hu retains source-supported xu. The f mapping is the reviewed site convention, not a quotation of the book.

componentPolicy: Record the full donor before considering a substring. Mixed words receive exact syllable spans and pronunciation-scoped notes.
